teaser.text: Coinbase Global runs platforms for digital assets—online items whose ownership and transfers are recorded on blockchains, shared electronic ledgers. It makes money by helping customers trade, store, move and use those assets, then sharing in the interest and fees generated around them.

paragraphs.text: By October 2029, the weighted price is $171.94, also down 1%. The final-date range is $167.43 in the bear case to $182.23 in the bull case, compared with today’s $173.16. The base case has the highest probability at 55%. The bear case has 30%, and the bull case has 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Coinbase?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit drives the scenarios. The base case starts at $480 million. It reaches $816 million and then $1,125 million. The bear case begins with a $416 million loss, then recovers to $174 million and $520 million. The bull case starts at $1,088 million and reaches $1,870 million before $2,600 million.

The bull case assumes revenue of $6,800 million initially and $10,000 million finally. Margins rise from 16% to 26%. That requires sustained derivatives growth, profitable subscriptions, USDC expansion and cost savings. Institutional transaction revenue already rose 48% year over year in H1 2026, partly because of Deribit, but H1 operating income was still negative.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Coinbase really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash left after ordinary operations and capital spending. If sustainable annual free cash flow were US$1 billion, its yield at this valuation would be about 2.2%. But paying employees with shares can preserve cash while reducing existing owners’ percentage of the company, so cash flow must be judged alongside compensation and dilution.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Coinbase today?

paragraphs.text: A forward P/E of 58.7x implies approximately US$2.95 of forecast earnings per share. Its inverse is an earnings yield of about 1.7%, which is not a cash return or a promise. Investors accepting that starting yield need meaningful growth, lasting profitability, or both.

earnings.title: Coinbase earnings date, guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: Coinbase's next results are October 29, 2026; management guides to expense ranges, while trading, margins and newer revenues are key tests.
earnings.opening: Coinbase's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether Coinbase turns newer revenues into durable earnings before rates, fees and dilution take them away.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Coinbase makes money, competes with rivals, is run by management, and faces its risks.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 2026 full-year adjusted expenses of US$4,200–4,450 million. It expects a US$600 million reduction against the 2025 annualized exit rate, an exit-rate comparison rather than a cut of that amount from actual 2025 spending. For Q3, subscription and services revenue guidance is US$500–580 million, while adjusted expenses are US$980–1,080 million. USDC rewards cost US$119.1 million in Q2 2026.

blocks.heading: What have Coinbase's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Investment movements explain the better-looking net result. June 2025’s reported profit of US$1,428,900 thousand shrinks to US$33,208 thousand under Coinbase’s investment-adjusted measure. June 2026 therefore combines a weak operating quarter with investment losses. Three consecutive revenue declines and a persistent adjusted operating loss do not yet describe a turn.

blocks.heading: What should Coinbase watchers look for in the next results?

paragraphs.text: Through 2027–2029, consumer spot volume, MTUs, fee mix and USDC balances decide earnings. Base and Coinbase One must show durable profit after costs, incentives, rewards and forgone trading fees. October 29, 2026 results test trading revenue, institutional activity, margins and the expense outlook. Buybacks must coexist with liquidity, lending needs and dilution.

The first dated test is the Q3 2026 result scheduled for October 29. A recovery in trading revenue, institutional activity and margins would move the forecast toward the base or bull cases; another operating loss would strengthen the bear case.
